issues.summary: greenBeanPull_impl_ persists the resummarize queue (greenBeanWriteQueue_) only as the LAST statement, after the up-to-5 weeklySummarize calls — but ingestSupplierRows (:575) has already written the new totals into Suppliers by then, destroying the snapshot diff the affected-week list was derived from. If the run throws or hits the GAS 6-minute limit anywhere in the :617-619 loop, the property still holds the PRE-run queue, so every week discovered by THIS run is lost permanently: the next run's snapshot now matches the sheet, no diff is produced, and those weeks' Summary figures stay stale forever. Failure scenario: first live run — the full ~13-week greenBeanWindow_ is new, so `affected` has ~13 entries; 5 are summarized and 8 are meant to be queued; the execution times out during summarize #4 (a full greenbean ingest via per-row appendRow plus 4 full Suppliers/Revenue/Summary read-modify-writes, each also opening the labour spreadsheet, is realistic near the 6-min cap); those 8 weeks never resummarize and weeklySummarize's own Monday run only covers the last completed week. The GREENBEAN_RESUM_CAP=5 cap exists precisely because the author anticipated the runtime limit, which makes this ordering a hole in that mitigation. Fix: write the full mergedUnique list to the property BEFORE the loop and rewrite the shrinking remainder after each weeklySummarize. Note the happy-path queue drain is tested (run1/run2/run3) but no failure-path test exists.

Step 5 enforced only HALF of the exclusivity it specified. validateIngest_ mechanically rejects kind='suppliers' + source='coffee_order_app' (the greenbean side), but the online-revenue side — step5.md item 6, 'no connector may POST online Shopify revenue' — was left as prose in docs/ingest-contract.md only: doPost still accepts kind='revenue' with channel='online' from any source. Because aggregateSupplierRows_ names online revenue groups by SOURCE, such a row makes weeklySummarize emit a SECOND Summary row (kind='revenue', location='online', same week, different supplier) alongside the shopify_orderapp row that shopifyWeeklyPull writes directly. doGet sums Summary, so the week's Roastery online revenue is double-counted — byte-for-byte the failure the v23/v24 cleanup exists to repair, with no detection anywhere. This is not hypothetical drift: test_code.js:4829-4839 sets up exactly that row pair and asserts 'the real "coffee_order_app" writer still gets its own Summary row', pinning the double-counting shape as intended. orderapp.gs:15-20 reasoned carefully about the OVERWRITE direction of this collision (hence the shopify_orderapp name) but never about the ADDITIVE one. Fix: extend the validateIngest_ guard to reject kind='revenue' + channel='online' (or at minimum + source='coffee_order_app'), and re-frame the case5 assertions.

The pre-ingest snapshot is keyed case-SENSITIVELY ('greenbean||' + String(existingRow[3]), :569, looked up at :589) while upsertRows_ matches keys case-INsensitively (rowKey_ lowercases, Code.gs:594). invoiceNum is passed through with casing preserved (Engine_CostApi.js:527 trims only). Failure scenario: someone retypes 'inv-700' as 'INV-700' in 06_Stock_Intake — upsertRows_ matches and updates the existing Suppliers row in place, but the snapshot lookup misses, the invoice is classified as NEW, and addAffectedWeek queues the week of the RECOMPUTED date instead of the stored one. If the two dates fall in different weeks, the wrong week resummarizes and the right one stays stale. Lowercase the snapshot key to match rowKey_.

greenBeanPull_impl_ calls orderAppRunSuccess_ — resetting the failcount AND stamping the staleness heartbeat — on any ok response, including one where the whole 3-month window matched zero rows. A live roastery returning rowsFetched:0 for a rolling quarter is a broken feed (renamed/emptied 06_Stock_Intake columns that still resolve, a from/to filter mismatch), but it reads as a perfectly healthy run: no alert, no log line, result.rowsFetched:0 goes nowhere. Same shape as shopifyWeeklyPull, which reports weeksFetched but nothing consumes it. Consider treating a zero-row full window as a non-success (or at minimum logging it loudly).

The round-1 money-signal fixes are Logger.log-only: excludedGross (:296), the flagged-row count (:552) and the upstream diagnostics.warnings (:461) all land solely in the GAS execution log, which nobody reads on a schedule, and only excludedGross/flaggedRows reach the return value (which is itself discarded by the trigger). The sibling shopSpend feed sets the precedent the other way — PRD-8 requires warnings[] to reach a tab/banner. This satisfies round 1's stated minimum ('at minimum log ... better, surface it the way PRD-8 mandates') but leaves an understated greenbean invoice or a refund-shrunk weekly figure with no path to Jake's attention.
